am_next: ⏭ live, but restart the app to see it
bfx_confirm: Tap again to run Battery Fix
bfx_desc: At the next reboot, Android’s stored battery statistics are reset, so the per-app usage history and learned capacity estimate start again from a full charge. This clears a skewed record; it does not add capacity or battery life. Available only at 100% on charge.
bfx_refused: Not available right now — needs 100% on charge
bfx_reset_fresh: Android has started a new record
bfx_reset_pending: Scheduled — applied at the next reboot
bfx_reset_wait: Android will write the new record by itself shortly
bfx_started: Scheduled: Android battery statistics will be reset after the reboot; no ART compilation is run
bfx_stopping: Recompiling stops after the current app
bfx_summary: 100% + charger. Recompiles apps; resets statistics after reboot.
cap_clamps_tip: How often the vendor thermal engine took the cap away from ASB: in the last hour, and since boot.
cap_period_none_tip: No vendor-held cap is active now. Historical polling samples are available only in detailed diagnostics.
cap_period_tip: One continuous vendor-held period can contain many polling samples. Raw samples remain in asbdiag and the infinite log report.
cap_tip_asb: The governor is holding the caps it computed.
cap_tip_clamp: The vendor thermal HAL is clamping below the requested cap.
cap_tip_raised: The vendor raised the ceiling above ASB’s for a moment - a launch or touch boost. That is not a limit, so the clamp counter beside it does not count it.
cap_tip_shell: Caps were written by the profile script.
cap_tip_thermal: A thermal overlay is in charge of the cap.
cap_tip_unknown: The cpufreq policy could not be read.

BG_TRIM_LEVEL.desc:
How strongly ASB holds back apps you are not using: rarely used apps go to stricter Android standby buckets. Calls, messages, alarms and the keyboard stay protected.

🔋 Battery life: Aggressive
🔔 Notifications on time: Off or Safe
✋ Not sure: Safe

descOpt.aggressive: Also stronger background and memory limits. Apps can lose their state or deliver notifications later.
descOpt.off: Android decides alone; standby buckets ASB changed are given back.
descOpt.safe: Rarely used apps go to stricter standby buckets; protected apps are never touched.

CAMERA_CONTRAST.desc: Adjusts the tone curve's contrast and saturation independently of Camera Grade. 3 is stock; higher values deepen shadows and strengthen colour, with 10 targeting 170% of the firmware scales. This does not raise Camera Grade's colour-matrix or detail multipliers. Reboot to apply. High values can clip shadow detail or make colours look unnatural.

CAMERA_GRAIN.desc: Controls grain added after noise reduction. 3 is stock, 0 removes this added grain, and higher values create an increasingly visible film texture; 10 targets 16× the shipped amount. ASB patches every addNoiseWeight* key present in the device's own tuning, including mode-specific variants. High values can look coarse in shadows. Reboot to apply.

CAMERA_LEVEL.desc: Scales the firmware's own photo/video colour, detail and sharpening values. 0 keeps stock tuning; 1–6 increase processing gradually, while 7–10 are deliberately strong and stylised. Device capability limits still apply. Level 10 targets up to 2.5× chroma, 3.4× AI blend and 3.5× sharpness before those clamps. Reboot to rebuild from the stock baseline. High levels can exaggerate noise or banding in deep shadows.

CAMERA_LOWLIGHT.desc: Controls separate sharpening scales for macro and low-light processing. 0 follows Camera Grade; higher values add a progressively stronger correction, with 10 targeting 3.2× before firmware limits. Close subjects and high ISO can make halos more visible. Raise this only when those modes are genuinely soft. Reboot to apply.

CAMERA_PORTRAIT.desc: Adjusts neural face and skin blending in supported portrait modes. Stock firmware may ship these weights at zero; higher levels can restore texture reduced by denoising, but can also make skin look artificial. Level 6 reaches the implemented blend-weight ceiling. Start at 1–2. This does not affect every camera mode. Reboot to apply.

CAMERA_PREVIEW_TNR.desc: Controls the camera's existing preview temporal noise reduction properties. Off can reduce preview processing at the cost of more visible noise; On requests stronger preview noise reduction. Stock restores the values captured before ASB first owned them. The properties apply live and are read back, but a successful write does not prove that every camera HAL mode honours them. Recorded-video quality or smoothness is not directly changed or guaranteed.
CAMERA_PREVIEW_TNR.name: Preview Noise Reduction

UX_ANIM_FORCE_RESTART.desc: A fallback for ROMs that ignore ordinary live animation-scale changes. Only a manual profile switch additionally restarts SystemUI; automatic profile changes do not. The screen may blink, the lock screen may appear, and overlays from other modules may close. It does not repair the scale value itself and is unnecessary when the ordinary path already has a matching readback.

UX_MANAGE_TIMEOUTS.desc:
Lets the ASB profile own two groups of timings: system animation duration and long-press/multi-tap windows. Performance shortens them; Battery restores stock values. This changes how quickly the UI responds visually, not app launch or computation speed. The separate Animation speed setting still works while this control is off.

🔋 Measured battery saving: not claimed
⚡ Shorter UI response: On
✋ Unsure: Off

descOpt.0: The ROM keeps its own timing; Animation Speed still works.
descOpt.1: Animation and touch timing follow the profile.

anim_speed.desc:
Sets Android’s window, transition and Animator animation scales. Profile delegates the choice to the active profile; a manual value applies independently. A smaller scale shortens visible transitions and zero disables animations; it does not accelerate apps or their rendering. If the ROM does not apply a change live, verify the readback before using the separate forced-restart option.

🔋 Battery: no guaranteed effect
⚡ Perceived speed: smaller scale
✋ Unsure: Profile

athena_service.desc:
OxygenOS's own background-app killer.

🔋 Battery life: Stock
🔔 Apps stay alive, notifications on time: Off
✋ Not sure: Stock

descOpt.off: Disable only AthenaService. Apps may stay active longer, with more RAM use and background drain.
descOpt.stock: OxygenOS keeps its normal Athena background policy.

athena_service.name: Athena Background Killer

audio_remove_volume_limit.desc: Removes Android's headphone volume ceiling so the existing slider can go higher; it does not add gain by itself. Off by default. This reduces a safety boundary, not just a warning: sustained loud listening can cause permanent hearing damage. Use the lowest comfortable level and limit listening time. Reboot if your ROM reads the policy only at startup.

audio_resampler.desc: Controls the quality of Android's sample-rate conversion when the source and output rates differ. Stock leaves the ROM unchanged; High and Max use longer, steeper filters, with Max costing the most CPU. Any audible difference depends on the recording and equipment and may be negligible. Playback already at the output rate, hardware-offloaded playback and Bluetooth codec encoding are not changed. Reboot to apply.

auto_battery_enable.desc:
Switches to the Battery profile when the charge gets low and back to your profile after charging.

🔋 Battery life: On
⚡ Performance: Off
✋ Not sure: On

descOpt.0: Your chosen profile stays at any charge level.
descOpt.1: Low charge switches to Battery automatically; charging restores your profile.

bat_suppress_gaming.desc:
In the Battery profile a game counts as ordinary heavy load instead of switching to the gaming state with its higher limits. Other profiles are not affected.

🔋 Battery life: On
⚡ Performance: Off
✋ Not sure: On

descOpt.0: Games get the full gaming treatment even in Battery.
descOpt.1: Battery stays a battery profile, also in games.

bt_a2dp_offload.desc:
Whether Bluetooth audio is encoded by the dedicated hardware block or by the CPU.

🔋 Battery life: Auto or On
🎛️ Bluetooth equaliser apps: Off
✋ Not sure: Auto

descOpt.auto: Leave the ROM's Bluetooth audio path unchanged.
descOpt.off: Use CPU encoding. This can let some equaliser apps process Bluetooth audio, with potentially higher CPU use.
descOpt.on: Request hardware/offloaded encoding where supported. Actual power use depends on the device and codec.

bt_link_stability.desc: Optional workaround for Bluetooth audio dropouts during playback. Stable suppresses Wi-Fi scanning while audio plays, which can help on devices where the two radios interfere. New networks may appear more slowly. No codec is forced and pairing is unchanged. Leave this off if your connection is already stable.
bt_link_stability.name: Bluetooth Link Stability

camera_hold_enable.desc:
While the camera is streaming, the governor keeps the CPU ceiling and cores instead of lowering them. Thermal and vendor limits still apply.

🔋 Battery life: Off
⚡ Performance: On
✋ Not sure: On

descOpt.0: Normal governor rules apply in the camera too.
descOpt.1: Smooth preview, bursts and recording; more power while the camera is open.

charge_aware_enable.desc:
While charging, ASB allows more performance when the battery is cool and backs off as it warms up.

🔋 Battery health: On
⚡ Performance: On
✋ Not sure: On

descOpt.0: Charging does not change the performance rules.
descOpt.1: More speed on a cool charger, less when the battery heats up.

cool_gaming.desc:
In games ASB starts cooling down earlier, at about 40 °C, instead of waiting for the usual sustained-load threshold.

🔋 Battery life / cooler phone: On
⚡ Performance: Off
✋ Not sure: On

descOpt.0: Games run under the normal profile and thermal rules until the phone is hotter.
descOpt.1: Less heat in long sessions; the frame rate can drop a little in demanding games.

disable_blur.desc:
Disables system window blur in the notification shade, notifications, volume panel and supported transitions, using an opaque background instead of live blur. This removes some compositor/GPU work, but the amount of saving depends on the scene and is not promised. Colors, transparency, refresh rate and animation timing are not directly changed. Some ColorOS builds need a reboot for every surface.

🔋 Less GPU work in supported windows: On
🎨 Original ColorOS material: Off
✋ Unsure: Off

descOpt.0: The ROM's blur stays.
descOpt.1: Solid backgrounds and slightly less GPU work; the compositor part may need a reboot.

documentsui_fix.desc: One-time repair for the system file picker on affected ColorOS/DSU setups. Enables and unhides DocumentsUI, resets its picker/files activities, and disables ColorOS File Manager for user 0. The File Manager returns on Off. Only states ASB changed are restored; nothing is re-applied at boot.
documentsui_fix.name: DocumentsUI / DSU Picker Fix

doze_level.desc:
How soon Android enters deep sleep (Doze) after the screen turns off. In Doze, background network, jobs and alarms wait for short maintenance windows; high-priority push still gets through.

🔋 Battery life: Moderate or Aggressive
🔔 Notifications on time: Stock
✋ Not sure: Night only

descOpt.aggressive: Target idle entry after two minutes and shorten selected sensing/location windows. Background work may be deferred.
descOpt.moderate: Target idle entry after five minutes with the screen off.
descOpt.night: Apply earlier Doze only during the learned sleep window.
descOpt.stock: Keep the ROM's Doze timing; remove the ASB override.

doze_trim_whitelist.desc:
Some installed apps are allowed to ignore deep sleep. Trimming takes user-installed apps off that list; the dialer, SMS, clock, root manager and the apps you keep in the list below stay exempt.

🔋 Battery life: Trim
🔔 Notifications on time: Leave alone
✋ Not sure: Leave alone

descOpt.0: The exemption list stays as the ROM and apps set it.
descOpt.1: User-installed apps follow deep sleep like all others; your kept apps and system essentials stay exempt. Leave alone or uninstall gives the list back.

dsp_loudness.desc: ASB DSP adds up to +30 dB of gain, with optional compression and a final sample-peak limiter. Start at +3 dB: high settings can sound heavily compressed even when peaks are limited. The first enable needs a reboot. DSP is bypassed in the external-EQ audio profile. On the speaker, gain is reduced when the battery reaches 42 °C and restored below 40 °C; wired and Bluetooth gains are not reduced by this rule. Values above +25 dB require DSP libraries rebuilt from this source; old prebuilts remain capped at +25 dB.

dsp_outputs.desc: Choose which outputs ASB DSP may process: the built-in speaker, wired headphones/USB DACs, or Bluetooth. Unavailable outputs are ignored. Off bypasses the whole DSP while preserving every level for later. Bluetooth processing can move playback away from hardware offload and increase screen-off CPU use; exclude Bluetooth if long listening sessions matter more than the effect.

dsp_voice.desc: Requires DSP Loudness. Two broad bands adjust voice body at 350 Hz and upper-edge sharpness at 3 kHz. Level 10 applies +5 dB and −6 dB respectively. This can make thin or harsh speech fuller, especially on the phone speaker; high values may sound unnatural. Start at 4–6 and use DSP Outputs to limit the effect to the outputs that need it. Changes apply live before the limiter.

feel_dc_dimming.desc: Controls the stock DC-dimming switch secure/display_dc_settings_switch. On a supported panel it can change low-brightness regulation and reduce visible PWM flicker; on an unsupported panel a successful key write proves nothing. ASB neither bypasses the brightness driver nor forces the panel. Low-brightness tint or gradient changes are possible and depend on ColorOS. Stock restores the saved original after readback.

descOpt.off: Disable this setting and verify the write by read-back.
descOpt.on: Enable this setting and verify the write by read-back.
descOpt.stock: Leave the ROM value untouched; after an ASB override restore the exact previous value.

feel_dc_dimming.name: DC Dimming System Switch

feel_game_memc.desc: Controls the stock game frame-interpolation switch secure/display_memc_game_enable. When the game and firmware support it, MEMC inserts intermediate displayed frames; it does not increase the game engine’s actual rendering FPS. Interpolation can add input latency, artifacts and energy use. Stock restores the saved original. A confirmed Settings write does not prove MEMC is active in every game.

descOpt.off: Disable this setting and verify the write by read-back.
descOpt.on: Enable this setting and verify the write by read-back.
descOpt.stock: Leave the ROM value untouched; after an ASB override restore the exact previous value.

feel_game_memc.name: Game MEMC

feel_gesture_mistouch.desc: Controls ColorOS accidental-touch protection through secure/gesture_mistouch_prevention_enable. It can reject some touches near curved-screen edges, for example when a palm holds the phone. This is not touchscreen calibration or a sampling-rate change; an aggressive ROM policy can also delay intended edge gestures. Stock restores the saved original, and readback confirms the write rather than recognition quality.

descOpt.off: Disable this setting and verify the write by read-back.
descOpt.on: Enable this setting and verify the write by read-back.
descOpt.stock: Leave the ROM value untouched; after an ASB override restore the exact previous value.

feel_gesture_mistouch.name: Gesture Mistouch Prevention

feel_pointer_speed.desc: Changes system/pointer_speed, which controls pointer movement for a mouse or trackpad connected to the phone. It does not change touchscreen sensitivity, touch sampling, gesture recognition or game speed. Stock does not overwrite another owner’s setting. On first explicit use ASB saves the current value and later restores that value; it is not necessarily the factory default. The result is verified through Settings. The saved baseline is the value captured when ASB first applied an override, not necessarily the factory default.
feel_pointer_speed.name: Pointer Speed

gms_freeze.desc:
Turns off single components inside Google Play services. Play services itself stays on, so push, sign-in, payments and the Play Store keep working. Each level includes the previous one.

🔋 Battery life: More
🧩 Every Google feature: Off
✋ Not sure: Safe

descOpt.max: Also on-device search indexing and background step counting. Some search results and background steps are missing.
descOpt.more: Also ad personalisation, location-history uploads and the backup scheduler. The Maps timeline stops recording.
descOpt.off: Every managed component back in its recorded original state.
descOpt.safe: Telemetry, usage statistics and analytics only; nothing you use depends on them.

gms_trim.desc:
Reduces Google Play services background work without turning components off.

🔋 Battery life: Strict
🔔 Notifications on time: Stock or Light
✋ Not sure: Light

descOpt.lite: Limit selected location and search-widget background work.
descOpt.stock: Leave Play services background scheduling under ROM control.
descOpt.strict: Also remove the Play services Doze exemption; push and sync may be delayed.

gnss_trim.desc:
Background apps get only coarse location while the screen is off and precise location again when opened. Navigation, fitness tracking, emergency and find-my apps are never trimmed.

🔋 Battery life: Trim
📍 Precise background tracks: Off
✋ Not sure: Off

descOpt.0: Apps keep the location precision they ask for.
descOpt.1: Background apps get coarse location with the screen off: fewer GPS fixes, less precise background tracks.

gnss_trim.name: Trim Background GPS

heavy_prime_escape.desc:
Smart only. When work keeps the prime cores at their ceiling on a cool phone, ASB lifts that ceiling briefly, never above Balanced, and then rests.

🔋 Battery life: Off
⚡ Performance: On
✋ Not sure: On

descOpt.0: The prime cores stay at Smart's ceiling: a little cooler, but long tasks take longer and keep the chip awake longer.
descOpt.1: Long heavy tasks (installs, exports, big pages) finish sooner; the lift stops by itself when the phone is warm.

heytap_mcs.desc: Off disables com.heytap.mcs for user 0 and verifies the resulting package state. Apps using HeyTap/OPPO Push can stop receiving notifications or receive them late; some apps may keep their own connection alive instead. Stock restores only the package state recorded by ASB. No system files are hidden or replaced.

descOpt.off: Disable HeyTap push transport with a package-state read-back. Check affected app notifications.
descOpt.stock: Leave MCS under Android/OEM control or restore only the package state recorded by ASB.

heytap_mcs.name: HeyTap MCS / OPPO Push

io_scheduler.desc:
Chooses only schedulers exposed by each block device. In the active Smart profile, Auto follows the existing bounded Smart scenario: ADIOS for gaming/heavy, Kyber for ordinary screen-on work, and mq-deadline for idle and none for screen-off, using discovered fallbacks. Outside Smart, Auto retains the profile policy. BFQ is never selected automatically; it remains an explicit experimental choice. Stock restores the exact per-device baseline. An unavailable explicit choice fails without substitution.

🔋 Smart idle: mq-deadline; screen-off/Battery: none first
⚡ Smart gaming/heavy: ADIOS first
✋ Not sure: Auto in Smart; Stock to leave kernel ownership

Scheduler selection alone does not prove better FPS, latency or battery life; compare on-device captures.

descOpt.adios: Preferred by Smart for gaming and heavy work when exposed. No UFS latency, FPS, throughput or battery gain is assumed.
descOpt.auto: In Smart, follow the live scenario with discovered fallbacks; BFQ is excluded. Other profiles keep their static Auto policy.
descOpt.bfq: Experimental manual-only choice. Auto never selects BFQ; stability and overhead depend on the kernel and workload.
descOpt.kyber: Preferred by Smart for ordinary screen-on work when exposed; a latency-oriented fallback for gaming/heavy.
descOpt.mq-deadline: A conservative choice preferred by Smart for idle and screen-off; no battery gain is assumed.
descOpt.none: No I/O reordering scheduler; can suit fast virtual or NVMe queues, but is not universally faster.
descOpt.stock: Restore the original scheduler independently for every block device.

io_scheduler.name: I/O scheduler

kernel_bore.desc:
BORE (Burst-Oriented Response Enhancer) changes how the kernel scheduler scores interactive and CPU-intensive tasks. On requests the BORE policy; Off disables it. Conservative Auto enables it only in Performance with fresh native thermal evidence and a normal active state, and otherwise restores the exact baseline. Stock restores the exact value this kernel had before ASB first changed it. This card appears as writable only when /proc/sys/kernel/sched_bore exposes 0 or 1 and permits root writes; every change requires read-back. No responsiveness, smoothness or battery gain is promised. In Smart, Auto instead follows the active scenario: light/heavy select 1; idle/conserve select 0, with read-back and the same exact baseline.

🔋 Battery life: Stock until measured on this kernel
⚡ Responsiveness: Auto or On can be tried; return to Stock if worse
✋ Not sure: Stock

descOpt.auto: Performance only: enables BORE with fresh native thermal evidence and a normal active state. Restores the exact baseline in other profiles, battery saver, low charge, heat, idle/gaming, Safe mode and watchdog recovery; missing or stale status follows that restore path, and with no baseline writes nothing. In Smart, Auto instead follows the active scenario: light/heavy select 1; idle/conserve select 0, with read-back and the same exact baseline.
descOpt.off: Writes 0 to disable BORE, then verifies the value read back from the kernel.
descOpt.on: Writes 1 to enable BORE, then verifies the value read back from the kernel. This is an experiment, not a guaranteed improvement.
descOpt.stock: Restores the exact 0 or 1 captured before ASB first changed this kernel; without an ASB baseline, writes nothing.

kernel_bore.name: BORE Scheduler

kernel_hrtimer_migration.desc:
Only for kernels with a separate switch for high-precision timers. Standard kernels, including 6.12 GKI, do not have one: then this card only shows the Timer migration value and writes nothing.

🔋 Battery life / ⚡ Performance: set Timer migration instead
✋ Not sure: Auto

descOpt.auto: Same rule as Timer migration: Off only in Performance.
descOpt.off: High-precision timers stay on their core.
descOpt.on: High-precision timers may move to a busy core.
descOpt.stock: Leaves the kernel's own value.

kernel_hrtimer_migration.name: High-resolution Timer Migration

kernel_lpm_prediction.desc:
Snapdragon CPU idle driver: besides the next timer, it uses the recent history of wake-ups to guess how long a core will really sleep. When interrupts keep waking a core early, it then picks a lighter sleep state instead of a deep one that would be left again at once; entering and leaving deep sleep costs energy and time. On newer kernels the switch is called prediction_disabled; the card still shows 1 = prediction on.

🔋 Battery life: On or Auto
⚡ Performance: On or Auto
✋ Not sure: Auto

descOpt.auto: On in the Battery profile, the kernel's own value in the others.
descOpt.off: No prediction: a core sleeps as deep as its next timer allows. More deep sleeps that end at once and slower wake-ups are possible; meant for diagnosis.
descOpt.on: Prediction on, as Snapdragon ships it. Fewer deep sleeps that are left again at once.
descOpt.stock: Leaves the kernel's own value (on Snapdragon normally On).

kernel_lpm_prediction.name: Idle Prediction (LPM)

kernel_mglru_min_ttl.desc:
Protects the memory of the apps you just used for 1 or 2 seconds, so it is not freed at once. If even that memory cannot be kept, the kernel closes an app instead of slowing the whole phone with endless reloading.

🔋 Battery life: Stock
⚡ Performance: 1000 ms (fewer freezes when RAM is full)
✋ Not sure: Stock

descOpt.1000: The value the kernel documentation suggests. Fewer freezes when memory is full.
descOpt.2000: Stronger protection. Background apps may be closed sooner.
descOpt.stock: The kernel's own value, usually 0 (no protection). Restored exactly as it was.

kernel_mglru_min_ttl.name: MGLRU Generation Protection

kernel_rt_boost.desc:
The minimum CPU speed that real-time threads ask for: sound playback and recording, screen composition, some camera threads and interrupt handlers. A higher floor gives them a faster start, which may help against crackling sound or dropped frames when the CPU runs slow, but costs power whenever these threads run. 1024 means full speed, 0 means only as fast as the load needs. Snapdragon phones usually set 0 at boot; ASB's CPU limits per app group still apply on top.

🔋 Battery life: 0 or Auto
⚡ Performance: 256 or Auto
✋ Not sure: Auto

descOpt.0: No extra boost. Lowest power; on a slow CPU these threads start from a low speed.
descOpt.128: A light floor for audio and camera threads. Small extra cost.
descOpt.256: A noticeable floor, for games and video recording. More power while these threads run.
descOpt.512: A strong floor. Only if crackling or stutter remains; the highest power use of these options.
descOpt.auto: Follows the ASB profile: Battery 0, Performance 256, the kernel's value in Balanced and Smart.
descOpt.stock: The kernel's value after boot (usually 0 on Snapdragon, 1024 on plain Linux).

kernel_rt_boost.name: Real-time Boost (Audio · Camera · Display)

kernel_sched_autogroup.desc:
A desktop Linux feature that groups processes by session for fair CPU sharing. Phone GKI kernels are built without it, so the card usually shows "not exposed" and nothing is written. Android already groups apps itself (foreground, background).

🔋 Battery life: Stock
⚡ Performance: Stock
✋ Not sure: Stock

descOpt.off: No session grouping.
descOpt.on: Groups tasks by session. Android's own app groups are not affected.
descOpt.stock: Leaves the kernel's own value.

kernel_sched_autogroup.name: Scheduler Autogroup

kernel_sched_child_runs_first.desc:
Who runs first after a process starts a new one: the new (child) process or the one that created it. A narrow setting that mainly affects how apps and services start. Newer kernels may no longer have this switch; the card then shows "not exposed".

🔋 Battery life: Stock
⚡ Performance: On can be tried for app starts; switch back if anything gets worse
✋ Not sure: Stock

descOpt.off: The process that started the new one continues first.
descOpt.on: The new process runs first. Can help some app launches.
descOpt.stock: Leaves the kernel's own order (normally the parent first).

kernel_sched_child_runs_first.name: Child Task Runs First

kernel_sched_nr_migrate.desc:
How many tasks the scheduler may move between CPU cores in one balancing step. Small numbers: short, light steps, but load evens out more slowly. Large numbers: load spreads faster, with more moving around.

🔋 Battery life: 2 or Auto
⚡ Performance: 8 or Auto
✋ Not sure: Auto

descOpt.1: Minimum balancing work; uneven load can stay longer.
descOpt.16: The most aggressive value offered; the most task moves.
descOpt.2: Light. A good choice for battery life.
descOpt.8: Spreads games and heavy multitasking faster.
descOpt.auto: Follows the ASB profile: Battery 2, Balanced and Smart 4, Performance 8.
descOpt.stock: The kernel's own value (usually 32).

kernel_sched_nr_migrate.name: Scheduler Migration Batch

kernel_sched_stats.desc:
Extra statistics the scheduler collects for debugging tools. Everyday use does not need them. Most kernels have them off already; then both choices are the same. Auto disables them only while Smart is active and releases the exact baseline in other profiles; Off disables them in every profile. Stock restores the kernel value. No measurable battery gain is promised.

🔋 Battery life: Off or Auto
⚡ Performance: Off or Auto
✋ Not sure: Auto

descOpt.auto: Auto disables debug accounting only in Smart and restores the exact baseline when another profile takes over.
descOpt.off: No debug statistics, so none of their small overhead. Restored on Stock or uninstall.
descOpt.stock: The kernel's own value. Choose it while diagnosing lag or scheduler problems.

kernel_sched_stats.name: Scheduler Debug Accounting

kernel_timer_migration.desc:
Decides who handles the timers of an idle CPU core. On (the kernel's default): a busy core takes them over, so idle cores can sleep longer. Off: every core handles its own timers.

🔋 Battery life: On or Auto
⚡ Performance: Off or Auto
✋ Not sure: Auto

descOpt.auto: Follows the ASB profile: Off in Performance, the kernel's value in all other profiles.
descOpt.off: Timers stay on their core. Can keep response steadier under heavy load; idle cores wake more often.
descOpt.on: Idle cores hand their timers to a busy one and sleep longer. The kernel's choice for saving power.
descOpt.stock: Leaves the kernel's own value (normally On).

kernel_timer_migration.name: Timer Migration

kernel_usb_autosuspend.desc:
How soon an idle USB device (DAC, headset, gamepad, flash drive) is put to sleep. Only matters while something is plugged into the USB port; charging is not affected.

🔋 Battery life: On
⚡ Performance: Stock
✋ Not sure: Stock. Choose Off only if a USB device keeps disconnecting or crackling

descOpt.off: USB devices plugged in afterwards never sleep. Fixes devices that drop out; uses more power while they are connected.
descOpt.on: Idle USB devices sleep after 2 seconds.
descOpt.stock: Leaves the kernel's own value (usually 2 seconds).

kernel_usb_autosuspend.name: USB Autosuspend

log_level.desc:
How much ASB and selected device logs record.

🔋 Battery life: Normal
🔍 Problem reports: Detailed
✋ Not sure: Normal

descOpt.0: Minimise device and ASB diagnostics. Later bug reports may lack the evidence needed for analysis.
descOpt.1: Record normal significant ASB events.
descOpt.2: Add learner updates and screen transitions; useful for battery investigations.
descOpt.3: Verbose diagnostics that grow quickly. Use only while reproducing a problem.
descOpt.stock: Do not change device logging through this setting.

lsposed_verbose.desc: Keep leaves LSPosed settings and logs under LSPosed's control. Off changes LSPosed's own Verbose log setting, removes old verbose-log files and takes effect after LSPosed restarts or the phone reboots. The modules log - what the LSPosed modules themselves write - has no switch in LSPosed, so while Off is selected ASB also clears it periodically. This can remove evidence needed to debug another module. If you later enable verbose logging in LSPosed, ASB does not reverse that choice; Keep restores ownership without secretly managing LSPosed.

descOpt.keep: Leave LSPosed settings and logs under LSPosed's control.
descOpt.off: Disable LSPosed verbose logging from its next start, remove old verbose logs and periodically clear the Modules log.

ltpo_force.desc:
Lets the panel drop its refresh rate when nothing moves and return to its top rate on touch, using a patched copy of the device's own refresh table and the selected idle-drop speed. Needs a reboot; the stock file is not changed. Rates below Android's advertised floor depend on the panel's own ADFR support.

🔋 Battery life: On; actual savings are device-dependent
⚡ Smoothness: Off
✋ Not sure: Off

descOpt.0: The ROM's refresh behaviour stays as shipped.
descOpt.1: The panel idles lower and returns to its maximum on touch; savings depend on the panel and ROM. Another module that owns the same table is left alone.

ltpo_force.name: Force LTPO Refresh

ltpo_idle_speed.desc:
How quickly the existing event-driven controller steps down after the last touch. Fast: 1 second before the first step and 1 second between modes. Balanced: 2 / 1 seconds. Gentle: 5 / 3 seconds. Touch immediately restores the panel maximum. Only modes advertised by this panel are used; a drop toward 1 Hz below Android's advertised floor remains dependent on the device's own ADFR table and is not guaranteed. Requires Force LTPO Refresh; no foreign table and no persistent polling worker.

🔋 Battery life: Fast may reduce idle refreshes; measure on this device
⚡ Smoothness: Gentle keeps higher rates through short pauses
✋ Not sure: Balanced

descOpt.balanced: Keeps the previous ASB timing: two seconds before the first step and one second between advertised modes.
descOpt.fast: Reaches the advertised idle floor sooner and can step down during short pauses; actual power use is device-dependent.
descOpt.gentle: Waits longer and steps down more slowly, preserving a higher refresh rate through short pauses.

ltpo_idle_speed.name: LTPO Idle Drop Speed

ltpo_peak_force.desc:
Works with Force LTPO Refresh: while you touch the screen, asks for the highest mode the panel reports (165 Hz on the OnePlus 15) instead of the ROM's 120 Hz for ordinary apps.

🔋 Battery life: Off
⚡ Smoothness: On
✋ Not sure: Off

descOpt.0: Ordinary apps keep the ROM's touch rate.
descOpt.1: Scrolling and touch run at the panel's top rate; more power while you touch.

ltpo_peak_force.name: Panel Maximum on Touch

ltpo_video.desc:
During video playback without touch, lowers the panel to the lowest mode that fits 30 or 60 fps content, such as 60 Hz. Touch, the end of playback or screen-off restores the previous rate.

🔋 Battery life: On
⚡ Smoothness: no effect on the video itself
✋ Not sure: On

descOpt.0: The panel keeps its usual rate during video.
descOpt.1: Fewer needless refreshes during video; the video's own frame rate does not change.

media_vol_steps.desc: Changes the number of media-volume positions without raising the maximum volume. More steps give finer control, especially at low listening levels. Stock keeps the ROM value; 20–100 selects a fixed count in steps of five. Reboot to apply. The saved slider position may then map to a quieter level, so check it once. Some ROMs ignore this setting; the action button and asbdiag report the value actually in use.

mglru_hold.desc: Protects the working set from reclaim so the foreground app is not evicted under memory pressure and rebuilt when you return to it. HOLD: 1 second of protection. AGGRESSIVE: 2 seconds - apps survive longer, less free RAM. Only has an effect on kernels with MGLRU; elsewhere the tweak does nothing.
mglru_hold.name: Keep Apps In Memory

mglru_mode.desc:
How the kernel picks which memory to free when RAM runs low. MGLRU is the newer method: it is designed to keep the apps you use in memory more reliably and to need less CPU work for reclaiming.

🔋 Battery life: Smart
⚡ Performance: On
✋ Not sure: Smart (the default)

descOpt.off: Old reclaim method. Only for comparison, or if something misbehaves with MGLRU.
descOpt.on: MGLRU with all its parts (7). Keeps apps in memory most consistently.
descOpt.smart: ASB switches between the lighter (5) and the full (7) variant by load. Some kernels accept only the base mode (1); then On and Smart work the same.
descOpt.stock: Leaves the kernel's own setting.

mglru_mode.name: MGLRU Mode

mmfeed_off.desc:
Closes the OEM multimedia feedback collector using a patched copy of the device's own list; the original file is not changed. Needs a reboot. Audio and video processing do not change.

🔋 Battery life: On
⚡ Performance: On
✋ Not sure: Off

descOpt.0: The collector runs as shipped.
descOpt.1: Less diagnostic logging and I/O; a saving is not guaranteed.

mmfeed_off.name: Multimedia Telemetry Off

net_congestion.desc:
How downloads ramp up on links the Wi-Fi and mobile cards do not cover: USB and Bluetooth tethering, VPN, Ethernet.

🔋 Autonomy: no universal winner
⚡ Performance: depends on RTT, loss, buffers and qdisc
✋ Not sure: Stock

descOpt.auto: The device's own algorithm stays (often cubic).
descOpt.bbr: Models bottleneck bandwidth and pacing; often useful on long or variable paths, but results still depend on queues and competing traffic.
descOpt.bbr2: A newer BBR variant with different loss/queue response; availability does not prove it is better than BBR for this route.
descOpt.bbr3: A newer BBR variant exposed by some custom kernels; behaviour is kernel-version dependent and not universally superior.
descOpt.bic: Loss-based predecessor of CUBIC; grows quickly on high-bandwidth-delay paths, but can react sharply to loss.
descOpt.cdg: Delay-gradient based and designed to back off around growing queues; real-world coexistence depends on the path.
descOpt.cubic: The common loss-based Linux default; robust general-purpose behaviour, with window reduction after loss.
descOpt.dctcp: ECN-oriented data-centre transport; not a general Internet choice unless the path and switches provide suitable ECN signalling.
descOpt.highspeed: Loss-based algorithm for very large bandwidth-delay products; more aggressive window growth can increase loss or queue pressure.
descOpt.htcp: High-speed loss-based variant that adapts growth using path history; not inherently lower latency.
descOpt.hybla: Designed for long-RTT/satellite-style paths; can be unnecessarily aggressive on ordinary short routes.
descOpt.illinois: Combines loss and delay signals for high-speed paths; queue response depends on accurate delay measurements.
descOpt.lp: Low-priority transport intended to yield to ordinary traffic; suitable for background flows rather than maximum foreground speed.
descOpt.nv: Delay-oriented New Vegas variant; can underperform when competing with aggressive loss-based flows.
descOpt.reno: Classic loss-based AIMD; predictable and conservative on high-bandwidth-delay paths.
descOpt.scalable: High-speed loss-based algorithm with scalable window growth; not a low-latency or power-saving policy.
descOpt.vegas: Delay-based algorithm that tries to avoid queues early; may yield too much against loss-based competitors.
descOpt.veno: Attempts to distinguish wireless/random loss from congestion; classification is not reliable on every modern path.
descOpt.westwood: Estimates bandwidth from the ACK stream and can suit some lossy wireless links; the estimate may be unstable on modern routed paths.
descOpt.yeah: Hybrid loss/delay algorithm aiming at fast paths with queue awareness; outcome depends on RTT and competing flows.

net_congestion_mobile.desc:
Download ramp for mobile data only. bbr often helps on mobile links with loss and changing delay.

🔋 Autonomy: no universal winner
⚡ Performance: depends on RTT, loss, buffers and qdisc
✋ Not sure: As global

net_lte_light.desc:
With the screen on, switches from 5G to LTE after three minutes of light traffic below 2 Mbit/s and back to 5G for heavy traffic. Not during calls, tethering, games or Wi-Fi.

🔋 Battery life: On
📶 Fastest mobile data: Off
✋ Not sure: Off

descOpt.0: 5G stays as Android chooses.
descOpt.1: 5G only while the traffic needs it; each switch can briefly re-register mobile data.

net_lte_light.name: 5G Only When Needed

net_mtu_probing.desc: For mobile or VPN routes where blocked path MTU discovery makes connections stall. On enables the kernel probe only after a suspected black hole; healthy routes keep their normal MSS. This is not a general speed boost. Stock and uninstall restore the exact previous 0, 1 or 2 value.
net_mtu_probing.name: TCP MTU Recovery

net_qdisc.desc:
How packets queue on links the Wi-Fi and mobile cards do not cover.

🔋 Battery life: no measurable difference
⚡ Low latency: fq_codel
✋ Not sure: Stock

descOpt.cake: The most queue management; costs a little more CPU.
descOpt.fq: Fair queue with flow pacing; pairs well with bbr.
descOpt.fq_codel: Keeps queues short under load: lower delay for games and calls.

net_qdisc_mobile.desc:
Packet queue for mobile data only.

🔋 Battery life: no measurable difference
⚡ Low latency: fq_codel
✋ Not sure: As global

descOpt.auto: Takes the value of the card for other links.
descOpt.cake: The most queue management; costs a little more CPU.
descOpt.fq: Fair queue with flow pacing; pairs well with bbr.
descOpt.fq_codel: Keeps queues short under load: lower delay for games and calls.

net_qdisc_wifi.desc:
Packet queue for Wi-Fi only.

🔋 Battery life: no measurable difference
⚡ Low latency: fq_codel
✋ Not sure: As global

descOpt.auto: Takes the value of the card for other links.
descOpt.cake: The most queue management; costs a little more CPU.
descOpt.fq: Fair queue with flow pacing; pairs well with bbr.
descOpt.fq_codel: Keeps queues short under load: lower delay for games and calls.

net_route_tune.desc:
The size of the first burst of a new TCP connection. A larger burst speeds up page loads and short downloads; on poor links it can cause retransmissions.

🔋 Battery life: Smart
⚡ Performance: Aggressive
✋ Not sure: Smart

descOpt.aggressive: Use a larger window; poor links may see more retransmissions.
descOpt.auto: Choose an initial route window from measured link conditions.
descOpt.off: Restore the route values recorded before ASB changed them.

net_rps.desc:
Which CPU cores may process received Wi-Fi packets.

🔋 Battery life: Stock or Little
⚡ Performance: All
✋ Not sure: Stock

descOpt.all: Allow receive processing on every CPU cluster; more cores may wake.
descOpt.little: Allow receive processing on the efficiency cluster.
descOpt.stock: Leave the kernel and driver receive-packet masks untouched.

net_rps.name: Spread Network Load

net_screen_off_lte.desc:
90 seconds after the screen goes off the phone prefers LTE instead of keeping 5G active; 5G returns when the screen turns on. Calls and heavy transfers keep 5G.

🔋 Battery life: On
📶 Fastest mobile data: Off
✋ Not sure: Off

descOpt.0: The network type does not change with the screen.
descOpt.1: Less 5G modem power in standby; each switch can briefly re-register mobile data.

net_screen_off_lte.name: LTE While Screen Off

net_txqueue.desc:
How many packets may wait in the Wi-Fi transmit queue. Shorter queues can cut delay under load but may limit throughput on fast or unstable links.

🔋 Battery life: no difference
⚡ Low latency (games, calls): Short
✋ Not sure: Stock

descOpt.short: Use 256 packets. Can reduce queued delay but may not suit every fast link.
descOpt.shorter: Use 128 packets. Test throughput, loss and latency under load.
descOpt.stock: Keep the driver's transmit-queue length.

net_txqueue.name: Transmit Queue

net_wifi_leave.desc:
Helps the phone leave a Wi-Fi network that is too weak or carries no traffic, by turning Wi-Fi off and on briefly while the screen is on.

🔋 Battery life: Weak signal
📶 Uninterrupted Wi-Fi: Off
✋ Not sure: Off

descOpt.aggressive: Use the fastest handover rules; Wi-Fi interruptions and mobile-data use are more likely.
descOpt.off: Do not actively leave Wi-Fi; Android and the driver control handover.
descOpt.unusable: Also act when a connected link carries no usable traffic.
descOpt.weak: Act when signal falls below −80 dBm.

net_wifi_leave.name: Leave Bad Wi-Fi

night_charge_enable.desc: Optional charging control for a custom interval. While charging inside the window, ASB uses a supported standard kernel control to hold around 80%; at the end it restores the exact previous value. Start is inclusive, end exclusive; windows may cross midnight, but equal endpoints are invalid. It never discharges a battery above 80%, does not replace OEM Adaptive Charging and is off by default. If no writable control exists, the status says not exposed. Disable, window exit or uninstall restores only values still owned by ASB.
night_charge_enable.name: Night Charge Limit

night_charge_end.desc: Local time when ASB restores the previous kernel value. End is exclusive and must differ from start; an earlier end crosses midnight.
night_charge_end.name: Charge window end

night_charge_start.desc: Local time when the optional 80% window begins. Start is inclusive; changing it reconciles charging immediately.
night_charge_start.name: Charge window start

night_modem_idle.desc:
In the learned night window, stretches mobile keepalives and quiets part of the modem data path so the modem can stay idle longer. Calls and SMS are not affected.

🔋 Battery life: On
🔔 Notifications on time: Off
✋ Not sure: Off

descOpt.0: Normal keepalives all night.
descOpt.1: Fewer modem wakeups at night; push and sync can wait until the next wake.

night_modem_idle.name: Quiet Radio at Night

night_quiet_enable.desc:
During a long screen-off stretch in the learned night window, the governor pauses its own non-essential periodic work. Apps and radios are not touched.

🔋 Battery life: On
⚡ Performance: no effect
✋ Not sure: On

descOpt.0: The governor keeps its normal schedule around the clock.
descOpt.1: Fewer governor wakeups at night.

perf_ceiling_pct.desc:
Caps the highest CPU and GPU speed ASB allows, as a share of the device maximum. Light work rarely reaches the cap; heavy work becomes slower but cooler. A lower cap does not always save battery: slower work keeps the chip awake longer.

🔋 Battery life: 85
⚡ Performance: 100
✋ Not sure: 100

phantom_procs.desc:
Android's limit on extra child processes that apps start outside their normal lifecycle: terminals, emulators, build tools. Restart the affected app after a change.

🔋 Battery life: Limit 32
⚡ Long background jobs: No limit
✋ Not sure: No limit

descOpt.relaxed: Disable the limit. Background child processes can survive, but runaway resource use is less contained.
descOpt.stock: Leave the current phantom-process setting untouched.
descOpt.strict: Explicitly set Android's limit to 32 phantom processes.

prime_escape_burst_s.desc:
How long one prime-core lift may last, in seconds. Used only while Prime Core Lift is on.

🔋 Battery life: 10
⚡ Performance: 30-40
✋ Not sure: 20

prime_escape_rest_s.desc:
How long ASB waits after a lift before the next one may start, in seconds. Used only while Prime Core Lift is on.

🔋 Battery life: 90-120
⚡ Performance: 20
✋ Not sure: 40

profile_class_auto.desc:
Fits the profile to the kind of app: Performance holds CPU ceilings at 80 % for a light app at ordinary load, Battery lifts them to at least 70 % for a game. Launches, heavy work, the camera and thermal limits are untouched.

🔋 Battery life: On
⚡ Maximum speed everywhere: Off
✋ Not sure: On

descOpt.0: Each profile applies its own ceilings to every app.
descOpt.1: Performance spends less on light apps; Battery gives games enough.

profile_class_auto.name: Profiles by Kind of Use

radio_policy_enable.desc: Independent master for ASB modem controls. OFF is the default: choosing any power profile leaves Android’s mobile-data context and TCP keepalive settings untouched. This is the recommended setting on WiFi-only or no-SIM devices. Turn it on only if this phone uses a SIM/eSIM and you deliberately want ASB’s separate radio options below. Turning it off immediately restores the Android values recorded before ASB changed them; it never changes airplane mode, carrier selection, roaming, preferred network type, Bluetooth or audio.
radio_policy_enable.name: Cellular / radio controls

smart_battery_bias.desc:
Nudges Smart toward Battery: 300 moves it 30 % of the remaining way from what it learned to Battery, 600 moves it 60 %. From about 400 Smart behaves almost like Battery in ordinary use. Halved during heavy work and games.

🔋 Battery life: 300-400
⚡ Performance: 0
✋ Not sure: 0

smart_lab.desc:
Smart tests more settings itself, one at a time next to the best one so far, and keeps a setting only when it measured cheaper without more janky frames, more time at the ceiling or faster warming. Smart profile only.

🔋 Battery life: On
⚡ Performance: On (a setting that makes things worse is not kept)
✋ Not sure: On

descOpt.0: Smart uses only what it has already learned.
descOpt.1: Smart keeps learning cheaper settings; results appear under What Smart learned.

smart_lab.name: Smart Lab

smart_lab_mem.desc:
Lets the lab also cap the CPU's votes on the memory bus while the screen is calm and in deep idle. Display, GPU, video and modem votes are never touched.

🔋 Battery life: On
⚡ Performance: Off
✋ Not sure: On

descOpt.0: The memory bus stays under the kernel's and the vendor's control.
descOpt.1: Memory-bus caps are tested and kept only when they measured cheaper.

smart_lab_mem.name: Smart Lab: Memory Bus

smart_media_guard.desc:
Smart only, for one case: a known video, feed or browser app stays as heavy as a game for a full minute on battery. ASB then holds the GPU at the existing media limit; games, charging and thermal protection are never limited.

🔋 Battery life: On
⚡ Performance: Off
✋ Not sure: Off

descOpt.0: Media apps get the GPU they ask for.
descOpt.1: Heavy video and feed sessions use less GPU power; a high-refresh stream can stutter.

smart_media_guard.name: Smart Media Guard

smart_records_balanced.desc:
In deep idle with the screen off, Balanced uses the screen-off CPU ceiling Smart measured as cheaper on this phone, when it is lower than Balanced's own. Nothing is tested under Balanced; ceilings are given back on wake.

🔋 Battery life: On
⚡ Performance: no effect with the screen on
✋ Not sure: On

descOpt.0: Balanced keeps its own screen-off ceiling.
descOpt.1: Balanced sleeps on Smart's measured screen-off ceiling.

smart_records_balanced.name: Balanced Uses Smart's Findings

sustained_temp_enter.desc:
Manual mode only: the CPU temperature at which ASB starts limiting long heavy load. Lower means earlier and cooler but slower; higher means more speed and more heat. The vendor's limits stay in force.

🔋 Battery life: 58-60
⚡ Performance: 68-70
✋ Not sure: 65

sustained_temp_mode.desc:
The temperature at which ASB starts holding performance back under long heavy load. The vendor's own thermal protection always stays active.

🔋 Battery life / cooler phone: Manual with a lower temperature
⚡ Performance: Smart
✋ Not sure: Smart

descOpt.manual: Use the temperature selected below without Smart adjustment.
descOpt.smart: Start from that point and allow bounded upward adjustment after qualifying sustained sessions.
descOpt.stock: Use the device trip point read from its CPU thermal zone at boot.

ui_effects_level.desc:
Chooses system-effect richness and the Recents presentation without changing screen resolution or refresh rate. Auto leaves the ROM alone; Stock uses its normal effects; Simplified reduces decoration and, on the supported OnePlus 15 build, switches Recents to a list and hides Cards/Simple. Availability depends on ColorOS; a successful settings write does not prove that the launcher accepted the presentation.

🔋 Fewer decorative effects: Simplified
🎨 Full ROM interface: Stock
✋ Unsure: Auto

descOpt.auto: Do not change the system's current effect level.
descOpt.flat: Simplify effects. Recents becomes a plain list and OxygenOS hides the Cards/Simple selector; OnePlus 15 only.
descOpt.stock: Use the device's normal effects and Recents presentation.

ui_nav_handle_autohide.desc: Controls automatic hiding of the bottom gesture handle through global/oost_navigation_handle_auto_hide. When enabled, the handle can disappear while unused; gestures, navigation buttons and touchscreen response are not changed by this setting. Stock leaves the ROM alone, while an explicit ASB change can be restored to its saved original. Success means a matching Settings readback; hiding behavior and support remain owned by ColorOS.

descOpt.off: Disable this setting and verify the write by read-back.
descOpt.on: Enable this setting and verify the write by read-back.
descOpt.stock: Leave the ROM value untouched; after an ASB override restore the exact previous value.

ui_nav_handle_autohide.name: Auto-hide Navigation Handle

ui_recents_corner_radius.desc: Changes Recents card rounding through the linked global/oost_recent_task_radius and oost_recent_task_radius_dp keys. 0 dp gives square corners; 32 dp is the strongest offered rounding. The master switch and dp value are applied and restored together; Stock restores the exact pair saved before ASB’s first change. ASB verifies Settings, not screen pixels: the active launcher may ignore these keys.

descOpt.0: Set the radius to 0 dp and enable the paired ColorOS radius master.
descOpt.12: Set the radius to 12 dp and enable the paired ColorOS radius master.
descOpt.16: Set the radius to 16 dp and enable the paired ColorOS radius master.
descOpt.20: Set the radius to 20 dp and enable the paired ColorOS radius master.
descOpt.24: Set the radius to 24 dp and enable the paired ColorOS radius master.
descOpt.28: Set the radius to 28 dp and enable the paired ColorOS radius master.
descOpt.32: Set the radius to 32 dp and enable the paired ColorOS radius master.
descOpt.8: Set the radius to 8 dp and enable the paired ColorOS radius master.
descOpt.stock: Leave the ROM value untouched; after an ASB override restore the exact previous value.

ui_recents_corner_radius.name: Recents Corner Radius

ui_recents_memory.desc: Shows or hides the memory-information line in Recents through secure/display_memory_information_recent_task. It only changes the displayed reading: it does not free RAM, evict apps or alter memory limits. Stock leaves another owner’s value alone; after an explicit change, ASB restores its saved original. Success requires a Settings readback, while actual visibility still depends on the ColorOS Recents panel.

descOpt.off: Disable this setting and verify the write by read-back.
descOpt.on: Enable this setting and verify the write by read-back.
descOpt.stock: Leave the ROM value untouched; after an ASB override restore the exact previous value.

ui_recents_memory.name: Recents Memory Indicator

ui_smooth_corners.desc: Controls the software smooth-screen-corner outline through global/smooth_corner_enabled. It changes corner styling, not the panel’s physical shape, refresh rate, brightness or touch response. Stock leaves another owner’s setting alone and restores the saved original after an explicit ASB change. Settings readback is verified; the visible outline depends on SystemUI, the theme and ColorOS support.

descOpt.off: Disable this setting and verify the write by read-back.
descOpt.on: Enable this setting and verify the write by read-back.
descOpt.stock: Leave the ROM value untouched; after an ASB override restore the exact previous value.

ui_smooth_corners.name: Smooth Screen Corners

wakelock_action.desc:
What ASB does with apps that keep the phone awake with the screen off. Measuring and the reports work either way.

🔋 Battery life: Act
🔔 Notifications on time: Watch only
✋ Not sure: Watch only

descOpt.0: Measure and report only; nothing is restricted.
descOpt.1: After 45 minutes awake with the screen off, an app that held the CPU for 10+ minutes and was not used today goes to Android's restricted bucket. System, mail, navigation and keyboards are excluded; nothing is force-stopped.

wakelock_fitness.desc:
Fitness and step-counter apps often keep the CPU awake in the background. Watch and band companions (Mi Fitness, Zepp, Galaxy Wearable, Fitbit and the like) are never touched: they keep notifications reaching your wrist.

🔋 Battery life: Limit, or Strict if the card says the ROM ignores it
🏃 Complete step and workout records: Protect
✋ Not sure: Protect

descOpt.limit: Android ignores their wakelocks, so they cannot keep the CPU awake alone. Step timelines and background workouts can have gaps; watch and band companions are excluded.
descOpt.strict: Like Limit, and for an app this ROM is seen ignoring the WAKE_LOCK limit for, also Android's own "Restricted" battery setting (background restriction). Its background work, syncing and step timeline can be delayed; the previous setting is handed back on Protect, Limit or uninstall.

wifi_country.desc: Selects the Wi-Fi regulatory domain, which controls the channels and transmit rules the driver may use. Stock keeps the value supplied by the device. CR explicitly selects the Costa Rica domain; it is not a universal speed setting, and availability still depends on the ROM, access point and hardware. Use only channels and power levels permitted in your actual location.

wifi_powersave.desc:
Wi-Fi power saving between packets: the radio dozes while no data flows.

🔋 Battery life: Screen off or Always
⚡ Performance: Off
✋ Not sure: Screen off

descOpt.always: Keep Wi-Fi power saving enabled during use and with the screen off.
descOpt.off: Keep the Wi-Fi radio awake between packets.
descOpt.screen_off: Enable Wi-Fi power saving only while the display is off.

wifi_powersave.name: WiFi Power Save

wifi_scan_throttle.desc:
How often ASB allows background Wi-Fi scans. Fewer scans mean less radio work while you stay in one place, but networks are found later. The active connection's speed does not change.

🔋 Battery life: every 10 or 30 minutes
📶 Finding networks quickly: unthrottled
✋ Not sure: every 5 minutes

descOpt.0: Suppress ASB-managed background scans; manual scans can still be initiated by the system or user.
descOpt.1: Allow a background scan about every 10 minutes.
descOpt.2: Allow a background scan about every 5 minutes.
descOpt.3: Allow a background scan about every 2 minutes.
descOpt.5: Allow a background scan about every 30 minutes; discovery can be much slower.

zygisk_enabled.desc: Master switch for attaching ASB to Zygisk in newly started app processes, or leaving them unattached after their next restart. Off preserves the selected mode, automatic app list, feature switches, guard and ART settings; enabling again restores that saved setup without silently choosing a new preset. The full control panel is on the ZYGISK page. Requires a Zygisk-capable root implementation. Safe mode and a broker failure fail open; existing apps are not killed.
zygisk_enabled.name: ASB Zygisk

zygisk_hints.desc: An accepted start/exit from the observer allowlist asks the existing governor for fresh evidence while the screen is on. At most 8 requests/minute, at least 2 seconds apart. Zygisk chooses no frequency, profile or app policy; thermal, dwell and vendor limits remain authoritative. Acknowledgement is not a boost or proof of power saving. LSPosed is never killed, hidden, frozen or throttled. The rate limit applies per active companion.
zygisk_hints.name: Zygisk Lifecycle Refresh

zygisk_launch.desc: When zygote starts a new process for the app you are opening (Android marks it as the top app), ASB hears it at once and covers the launch with the unlock lift: a running lift is carried over the start, otherwise one is armed even inside the 5-second anti-chatter gap. No package name is sent; profile, thermal, warm-die and lift-length rules still decide. At most one cold start per second and 20 per minute; costs one short companion connection per cold start. Needs the Zygisk Process Observer switch, not the allowlist. Faster cold starts are expected, not proven: compare `am start -W` times with this on and off.
zygisk_launch.name: Zygisk Cold-Start Lift

zygisk_ledger.desc: Counts, for this boot, how many processes each ordinary app starts with the screen off and on. Apps that keep starting work at night are a common hidden battery drain; the top ones appear in Device diagnostics and asbdiag. Package names and counts only, kept in memory (tmpfs); nothing is restricted automatically. Costs one short companion connection per app process start while on. Needs the Zygisk Process Observer switch.
zygisk_ledger.name: Zygisk Process-Start Ledger

dsp_true_peak.name: DSP True-Peak Limiter
dsp_true_peak.desc: 4x oversampled inter-sample peak detection. Requires a rebuilt advanced-v1 DSP library.

dsp_lookahead.name: DSP Look-ahead
dsp_lookahead.desc: PCM delay in ms; zero adds no latency. Unsupported rates fall back to zero.

dsp_dc_protect.name: DSP DC / Infrasonic Protection
dsp_dc_protect.desc: 20 Hz high-pass before tone stages. Requires advanced-v1 DSP.

bt_ldac_quality.name: LDAC Playback Quality
bt_ldac_quality.desc: Keeps the LDAC quality you pick after every reconnect, instead of falling back to adaptive bitrate. It is the same setting as Developer options, applied again when the headset connects or the codec changes, and read back afterwards. Nothing changes for AAC, aptX, SBC or LHDC, or for headsets that do not use LDAC. 990/909 kbps needs a clean radio link; on a busy link it can stutter, then choose 660/606 or adaptive. A small background helper stays resident while a fixed quality is selected; Auto removes it.

bt_ldac_rate.name: LDAC/LHDC Sample Rate
bt_ldac_rate.desc: Keeps the LDAC sample rate you pick after every reconnect and reboot, instead of the 48 kHz Android often falls back to. It is the sample-rate choice from Developer options, asked for again when the headset connects or the codec changes, and read back afterwards. A rate the headset does not offer (greyed out in Developer options) is never forced: the current one is kept. It works on LDAC and on any other codec that offers the rate, such as LHDC; other codecs keep their rate. 96 and 192 kHz need more bandwidth; if the sound stutters, pair them with 660/606 or adaptive quality. Auto removes the helper when LDAC quality is Auto too.

cpu_vendor_unlock.name: Vendor CPU Ceiling
cpu_vendor_unlock.desc:
OnePlus/OPPO ROMs keep a second, lower CPU ceiling of their own - on some phones the fastest cores are held near 60 % of their maximum - plus another one while a game runs. ASB lifts both to each core's own hardware maximum, which mostly helps single-core bursts: app starts, page loads, compiling. Performance profile lifts them only while Performance is selected; Always in every profile except Stock; Off never. ASB's own heat limits and the kernel's thermal protection stay in force, and the vendor values are handed back unchanged when the lift ends. Qualcomm only. Do not combine it with another module that lifts the same ceiling: ASB then stays out of the way.

🔋 Battery life: Off
⚡ Performance: Performance profile
✋ Not sure: Performance profile

dev_evidence_note: Unknown, not exposed and not runtime-discoverable are collection limits, not proof that the device lacks support.
dev_grp_asb_guide: ASB runtime state and only the device capabilities ASB actually discovered.
dev_grp_hw_guide: Physical components and their live readings. Current limits are evidence, not proof of who set them.
dev_grp_kernel_guide: Build configuration and runtime facilities are separate kinds of evidence.
dev_grp_root_guide: Root and metamodule interfaces detected at their exposed paths.
dev_grp_sw_guide: Build identity, uptime and memory reported by Android and procfs.
dev_guide_adios: ADIOS schedules block I/O; BORE schedules CPU tasks. Build config and symbols do not prove runtime selection. Queue scheduler lists show exposure, and [adios] shows actual selection. No latency, throughput or battery gain is inferred.
dev_guide_asb_caps: Only exposed, discovered control paths are listed. Missing evidence is not proof that the hardware lacks a feature.
dev_guide_asb_properties: Static and validated managed properties are listed separately. Selected means the corresponding ASB owner and feature block were active; readback compares the live value. A mismatch is not rewritten here. Other unrelated Android/vendor properties are not dumped.
dev_guide_cpu_policy: Current limits and the hardware range are different. A current limit alone does not identify ASB, the vendor or another writer.
dev_guide_kernel_bore: CONFIG_SCHED_BORE is build evidence; /proc/sys/kernel/sched_bore is the runtime interface. This read-only diagnostic never writes it. The separate Kernel setting accepts Stock, conservative Auto, Off and On; an apply is successful only after read-back.
dev_guide_kernel_btf: BTF config, vmlinux exposure and module entries are separate facts. No BTF program or probe is loaded by this read-only page.
dev_guide_kernel_ebpf: Config and bpfs/sysctl exposure do not prove that eBPF is active. No program is loaded to test the syscall.
dev_guide_kernel_external: Not observable means this read-only snapshot cannot determine external kernel or undervoltage state; it does not prove stock voltage.
dev_guide_kernel_features: Config flags, exposed interfaces and positive runtime evidence are separate. /proc/config.gz may be a stock compatibility/spoofed payload; a loaded module, a named kernel symbol or an existing CAKE qdisc takes precedence over a contradictory config. CAKE and Sched Stats expose their supporting evidence separately. Collection is read-only: no module is loaded and no qdisc, sysctl or sysfs state is changed. Missing evidence means unknown or not runtime-confirmed, not proven disabled.
dev_guide_kernel_fuse_bpf: FUSE-BPF needs its own positive evidence. Ordinary FUSE, generic eBPF or a connection count alone is insufficient.
dev_guide_kernel_origin: Stock-like and custom-like describe exposed indicators, not a guaranteed builder or provenance. Capability decisions still use each exposed control node.
dev_guide_lsposed_hooks: LSPosed does not count individual hook calls or their energy, and ASB adds no hook of its own to measure them. This card joins evidence per hooked app: enabled modules and their scope, LSPosed log volume and errors, crash and ANR records whose stack passes through a hook, CPU time of hooked apps and restart loops from the Zygisk start ledger. A finding is a correlation to check by disabling one module for one app, not a proven cause.
dev_guide_memory: MemAvailable estimates memory available for new work. Cache is reusable and is not simply wasted memory.
dev_guide_root: The KSU interface family and the exact root implementation are separate facts. A variant is named only when version evidence names it.
dev_guide_system_load: A bounded 0–100 pressure heuristic from measured components only. Missing components are excluded and weights are renormalized; below 40% coverage the result is unknown. This is not device health, a trend, or an A/B comparison. With pressure stall information (PSI) the score uses the time tasks waited for the CPU, memory and storage instead of load average and the share of memory in use.
dev_guide_zygisk_observer: Process telemetry plus an optional bounded request for fresh governor evidence. Configuration, injection evidence, hint acknowledgement and overhead are separate facts. Missing crash/ANR attribution and app activity sources remain unknown or not exposed.
dev_guide_zygisk_provider: Provider identity is read from installed module name/version metadata. Enabled, disabled and pending-removal states are separate. Module metadata does not prove which provider is active in the running Zygote; companion events do not identify a provider.

doze_keep_copy: Ticked apps stay exempt from Doze: ASB never trims them, and if Android has no exemption for one, ASB gives it. Tick the messengers, mail and VPN whose notifications must arrive on time at night. Changes apply when this window closes.
doze_keep_day: Deep Sleep is set to night: ASB trims only inside the sleep window (%s). It is closed now, so every trimmed app is back and Trimmed stays empty until tonight. Ticked apps keep their exemption day and night.
doze_keep_legend:
Exempt - Android itself has this app exempt: you allowed it (Battery > Unrestricted) or the app asked for it. ASB has not touched it.
Exempt via ASB - Android had no exemption for it; ASB gave one because you ticked the app. Untick it and ASB takes it back.
Trimmed by ASB - the app was exempt and ASB took the exemption away. Tick it and the exemption comes back.
Never trimmed - kept by ASB's own rules: authenticators, Bluetooth, watches and bands, caller ID.
Ticked - your list: ASB never trims these apps and keeps them exempt.
Trimmed - the apps ASB has taken the exemption from right now. With Deep Sleep on night this list fills only inside the sleep window.
doze_keep_nolabel: This root manager does not give app names to the page - search by package name, for example telegram or whatsapp.

kc_why_io_scheduler: No readable non-rotational block-device queue exposes a scheduler list, or the queue is read-only. ASB does not create a generic sysfs writer or claim support.
kc_why_kernel_bore: This kernel exposes no /proc/sys/kernel/sched_bore control. CONFIG_SCHED_BORE or an install-log line alone does not prove a runtime interface. ASB writes nothing.
kc_why_kernel_lpm_prediction: This kernel exposes neither lpm_prediction of the older lpm_levels driver nor prediction_disabled of the qcom-cpu-lpm governor. ASB writes nothing; the diagnostic export lists the idle-driver parameters this kernel has.
kc_why_kernel_rt_boost: This kernel has no sched_util_clamp_min_rt_default: it is built without CONFIG_UCLAMP_TASK. ASB writes nothing.
kc_why_kernel_sched_autogroup: This kernel has no autogroup switch. GKI kernels are normally built without CONFIG_SCHED_AUTOGROUP because it changes signal_struct, which vendor modules are compiled against; ASB does not work around that. Even when built in, it would regroup only tasks left in the root CPU cgroup, and Android places app tasks in its own CPU groups.
kc_why_kernel_sched_nr_migrate: Needs a kernel built with scheduler debugging (CONFIG_SCHED_DEBUG) and debugfs. ASB mounts debugfs privately only for the moment it reads or writes the value, so nothing more is needed when both are built in.
kernel_absent_autogroup: Scheduler Autogroup is hidden: this kernel has no such switch (GKI kernels are built without it), and on Android it would not touch apps anyway, because they run in Android's own CPU groups.
kernel_absent_hrtimer: High-resolution Timer Migration is hidden: this kernel has no separate switch for it. Timer migration above already moves high-resolution timers too, so setting that one is enough.

lr_detail_cpu_peak: The highest sampled CPU thermal reading in this capture, not the average temperature and not proof of sustained throttling. The duration above 45 °C and the named hottest phase below show how long and where heat actually persisted.
lr_detail_drain: Battery percentage lost divided by eligible off-charger time. Charging is excluded. The estimate from a full charge is only this capture’s pace projected forward, not a promise of battery life or proof that a tweak caused the result.
lr_detail_drain_windows: The total is a sum of separate windows between charging sessions, so it can exceed 100%. It is not the drop of one battery charge.
lr_detail_idle: This is the longest eligible quiet screen-off chain, not the average of every short pause and not necessarily a whole night. Deep sleep is the share when the device was not awake. Short chains and whole-percent battery steps can make the rate noisy.
lr_detail_idle_floor: A stable verdict needs an idle chain of at least two hours.
lr_detail_jank: The share of sampled frames that missed their deadline. It describes rendered frames in this capture; it does not by itself identify whether the app, ROM, thermal state or ASB caused the delay. Use the per-app and wake-window breakdown below.
lr_detail_jps: Janky frames divided by sampled frame time. Unlike a percentage, this also reflects how often a visible hitch occurred. It is an observed smoothness metric, not an FPS average or proof that changing a ceiling will improve it.
lr_detail_skin_peak: The highest sampled surface or skin-sensor reading. It is closer to how warm the phone feels than the CPU die peak, but it is still a snapshot maximum. The time above 40 °C below is the useful duration evidence.
lr_details_note: Measured values behind the summary. Rates apply only to their stated windows.
