lvb_cold_tip: Battery under 5 °C and under 40 %: lower CPU peaks until it warms up or charges.
lvb_lowbat_tip: Low battery: Smart leans to economy until the phone is charged.
lvb_smooth_on_tip: A little more CPU headroom made this app smoother in a test and is kept for it.
lvb_smooth_test_tip: This app misses frames: Smart is testing whether a little more CPU headroom helps.
lvi_alpha: How far the current policy leans from {bal} toward {bat}, in percent, learned from what this slot usually costs. 0% is {bal} behaviour; higher values hold the phone back more to save charge. Heat, a game or a camera session pushes it back down on its own.
lvi_apphint: What the foreground load looks like right now: “{app0}”, “{app1}”, “{app2}”, “{app3}” or “{app4}”. Smart reads it from the app in front and the load it creates, and gives games and heavy work more frequency headroom than a messenger.
lvi_basis: What steers Smart right now. Usually the records for the situation you are in: “{rec}” - a setting cheaper than the original one by the share shown was found, checked by pairs of measurements; “{rok}” - the original setting is already the best; “{trial}” - a neighbouring setting is being tried, pairs done of pairs needed. “{smt}” / “{smo}” - this app’s smoothness is being tested, or the extra headroom that helped it is kept. While this time slot has little history, the tile shows where Smart borrows from: “{fb1}”, “{fb2}”, “{fb3}”, “{fb4}”. Protection comes first: “{cold}”, “{lowb}”, “{brief}”, “{night}”, “{guard}”. Below: the records of every situation.
lvi_battemp: Battery temperature. Above about 40 °C charging slows down and the battery ages faster; above about 45 °C the system limits performance to protect it.
lvi_board: Temperature of the main board under the shell. It sits between the CPU and the shell and shows heat soaking into the phone: after a game or a long charge it stays high even when the CPU has already cooled.
lvi_capsrc: Who set the CPU frequency ceiling right now: “ASB” - the profile and Smart; “Vendor” - the OnePlus thermal or performance service; “Thermal” - a thermal overlay; “Shell” - the profile script, for a few seconds after a switch until the governor takes over again. When the vendor holds a lower ceiling ASB leaves it alone rather than fighting it. “Vendor ↑” - the vendor briefly raised the ceiling above ASB’s (a launch or touch boost); that is not a limit and is not counted as one.
lvi_clamps: How often the vendor service pushed the ceiling below what ASB asked for: in the last hour, and since ASB started. A few an hour is normal; dozens mean a hot phone or an aggressive vendor mode.
lvi_conf: How much Smart trusts what it has measured for this slot. The figure grows with every stretch of use; while it is low, Smart leans on neighbouring slots and safe defaults instead of guessing from a handful of samples.
lvi_cpu: Temperature of the CPU cores. ASB steers by one core sensor that it checks against its neighbours, so a stuck zone is never trusted; in Stock it is the hottest core. Up to about 45 °C is cool, short spikes when an app opens are normal, and throttling starts around 60 °C held for a while.
lvi_cpuceil: How much of the hardware maximum the ROM lets the CPU reach right now, on the most limited cluster. In Stock ASB sets no ceilings, so anything under 100% here comes from the OnePlus thermal or performance service.
lvi_fsm: What ASB thinks the phone is doing: DEEP_IDLE - asleep with the screen off, LIGHT_IDLE - screen on with nothing to do, MODERATE - ordinary use, HEAVY - an app launch or a heavy page, SUSTAINED - long heavy work with heat, GAMING - a game. Each state has its own frequency ceilings.
lvi_gauge_real: This phone's current sensor reads about %1× low (%2 checks): the real draw is nearer %3 mA, about %4 %/h
lvi_gauge_real0: This phone's current sensor reads about %1× low (%2 checks): the real draw is nearer %3 mA
lvi_gpu: How busy the graphics processor is, as a share of time. Scrolling and video sit around 5-30%, games at 50-100%. A game state is entered only when the load stays high, not on a single spike. The small figure is the clock: a high share at the lowest clock - this page drawing itself, for example - is light work, and the colour follows busy share × clock.
lvi_gpuclk: The graphics clock at this moment. It drops to the minimum when nothing is drawn and climbs with load; in Stock ASB does not touch it.
lvi_headroom: How much of the CPU hardware maximum the current ceilings allow, on the most limited cluster. 100% means nothing holds the CPU back. A low figure on a cool phone is a profile or vendor limit, not heat.
lvi_hist_wait: The history of this reading builds up while Monitor stays open.
lvi_learner: How many stretches of use (“{ses}” on the tile) Smart has learned from, across all twelve slots. Every 20 minutes of use and every night adds one. The more there are, the more Smart decides from measurements of your phone instead of defaults.
lvi_learner_prof: How many sessions of this profile (“{ses}” on the tile) the governor has learned from. Each records how long the phone took to warm up, how hot it got and how well the ceilings held; the profile’s thresholds adapt from them. On Battery the tile also rates the last session: clean, partial, noisy or disturbed.
lvi_learnpause: In Stock Smart neither learns nor decides - the ASB frequency policy is off. Everything it has learned is kept and is used again as soon as you switch back to Smart.
lvi_lpm: The modem’s power mode, read from the governor’s own state file: “{lnormal}” follows the profile; “{lsave}” lets the radio idle with stretched keepalives (screen off or the {bat} profile); “{lfast}” keeps latency low for games and downloads; “{lnight}” stretches idling further inside the night window Smart learned from your routine.
lvi_pressure_failed: The system load could not be measured right now.
lvi_sbattery: Charge level and voltage, read straight from the battery driver. The voltage falls as the charge goes down and sags briefly under load; below, the battery temperature.
lvi_sclock: The highest current clock among the CPU clusters in this reading. It changes many times a second, so one reading says little on its own; below, the clock of every cluster.
lvi_scr_wait: Screen-on and screen-off time appear after the next restart: they are counted from the moment the phone starts.
lvi_sdrain: The current flowing out of the battery right now, read straight from the battery driver. It jumps with every tap and falls when the screen goes off - the hourly drain with the screen on and off is in the two tiles above. Below: this current as an hourly rate.
lvi_skin: Temperature of the shell - what your hand feels. It moves slowly and trails the CPU by minutes. Up to about 38 °C feels neutral, above about 42 °C the phone feels warm, and around 45 °C the system starts holding performance back.
lvi_sload: System load over the last minute: how many tasks were running or waiting - for the CPU or for storage - on average. Android counts storage waits too, so this number alone can read past the core count on a phone that is doing almost nothing; that is normal, not an overload. The percentage beside it is the part of the last seconds the cores were genuinely busy, measured from /proc/stat between two readings. The 5- and 15-minute figures and the per-core share are in the tooltip.
lvi_slot: Smart splits the day into six parts - {dp0} 0–6, {dp1} 6–9, {dp2} 9–12, {dp3} 12–17, {dp4} 17–21, {dp5} 21–24 - kept apart for weekdays (“{wd}”) and weekends (“{we}”): twelve slots, each with its own measurements. This is the slot the phone is in now. What a workday morning costs is not spent on a Sunday morning.
lvi_slotheat: Not the temperature now - how warm this slot usually runs. Smart remembers the CPU peak of every stretch of use in each slot and compares this slot with the phone’s own norm, the middle of all its slots: “{hcool}”, “{hnorm}” or “{hwarm}”. A slot that usually runs warm gets slightly gentler ceilings in advance, before the phone heats up; one that runs cool gets a little headroom back.
lvi_slpm: Whether the ROM keeps mobile data up while Wi-Fi is connected (the “mobile data always active” developer setting): “{lfast}” - kept up, a faster handover for a little more drain; “{lnormal}” - the ROM’s default. In {stock} ASB applies no modem policy; this is the ROM’s own setting.
lvi_sram: Memory available to apps right now without closing anything, next to the phone’s total. Android keeps apps in memory on purpose, so a low figure is not a problem unless apps keep restarting.
lvi_strend: Where the CPU temperature is heading, from ROM readings every 10 seconds over the last two minutes: “{up}”, “{fl}” or “{dn}”. In {stock} nothing in ASB reacts to it; it shows what the phone’s own thermal management is working against. For the first half-minute after Monitor opens it is still measuring (…).
lvi_suptime: Time since the phone was last started. Below: when that was, and how long the screen was on and off since then.
lvi_trend: Where the phone’s temperature is heading: “{up}”, “{fl}” or “{dn}”. A warming trend makes Smart back off before a hard thermal limit is reached; cooling gives the headroom back. Right after a profile switch the trend stays muted for two minutes, so a stale reading cannot steer the new profile.
lvi_trend_chart_wait: The diagram appears after two temperature readings in the same window.
lvi_trend_rate: %1 °C per minute over the last %2 s
lvi_zram: Compressed memory (zRAM) in use. Android packs apps you have not used for a while here instead of closing them. Several GB is normal with many apps open; it costs CPU time only when an app is unpacked again.
lvi_zram_use: Compressed memory (zRAM): %1 of %2 GB in use
lvp_basis_load: This kernel exposes no pressure stall information, so load average and the share of memory in use stand in; both read high on an idle Android phone.
lvp_basis_psi: Measured as the time tasks waited for the CPU, memory and storage over the last 10 s, plus the CPU and GPU work right now.
lvp_vs_class: This is pressure on the whole phone, including this page drawing itself; the load class above is what the app in front asks for, so the two can differ.

soter_auto_note: After the first unlock, waits 90 seconds and runs a repair pass, then waits 60 seconds and runs one more bounded pass when automatic repair is still enabled and storage remains unlocked. Each pass can clear and restart the SOTER server twice. Completion means only that the reset/service workflow finished: check AfterSale → Key Status → SOTER key for physical PASS. A notification reports this distinction. Every clear creates new SOTER keys, so fingerprint payment has to be switched on again in affected apps.

soter_desc: SOTER is the Tencent key server behind fingerprint payments in WeChat Pay, Alipay and many Chinese banking apps. If those apps report a failed device check although everything else works, the repair stops the SOTER service, clears only the SOTER server data so it creates fresh keys, and starts the service again. Afterwards switch fingerprint payment on again in those apps. It does not hide root or an unlocked bootloader. A successful clear and running service do not prove a physical PASS: confirm the key in AfterSale → Key Status → SOTER key.

zy_auto_note: Only user-installed apps enter the observation list. Turning automatic setup off restores the previous app list, observer settings, guard and ART state. Safe mode is never cleared automatically. No LSPosed, kernel, frequency or thermal setting is changed.
zy_auto_profile_note: Observe: ledger only. Launch: cold-start assist and ledger, without AppOps. Battery: guard after two separate session observations and your per-app confirmation; no ART.
zy_auto_recommended: Choose one policy · no package lists to fill in
zy_auto_safe: Safe mode is on. Automatic setup will not clear it; clear Safe mode explicitly first.
zy_auto_summary: Profile: %1 · %2 observed app(s) · Background guard: %3 · ART (independent): %4
zy_control_failed: Zygisk setting was not changed; check the current state
zy_controls_note: These switches fine-tune the current mode. A mismatch is shown as Custom and is never silently rolled back. Master, cold-start and ledger changes affect newly started or restarted app processes.
zy_feature_master_off_why: Enable ASB Zygisk connection to change this feature. Its saved value is preserved.
zy_guard_approved: Package confirmed; two-session evidence is still required
zy_guard_bg_note: Process starts the user did not ask for, summed across reboots since the guard was switched on: starts with the screen off plus starts with the screen on minus the ones as the app in front. Every one wakes the CPU and initialises the app.
zy_guard_bg_row: %1 in the background · %2 with the screen off · opened %3
zy_guard_confirm_desc: Before an automatic AppOps restriction ASB requires the same evidence in %s separate screen sessions and your confirmation for that package. A proposal changes nothing yet. Restrictions can delay background work and notifications; Give back now restores the recorded mode immediately.
zy_guard_desc: With the screen off, an app that starts again and again (%s or more process starts in 5 minutes, counted by the Zygisk start ledger) gets its background activity restricted until the screen turns on; then the previous setting comes back. Messengers, mail, alarms, navigation, watches, VPN and the apps on the Doze keep list or in the notification fix are never touched.
zy_guard_desc_screen_on: With the screen on, an app whose background processes - not the app in front - start %s or more times in 5 minutes while nothing of it is visible is restricted for 30 minutes, and given back at once when you use it.
zy_guard_desc_wakers: Loops + night wakers: an app whose process starts %s or more times during one screen-off period, at any pace, is restricted the same way until the screen turns on. Each restriction counts the starts that still happened while it was in place.
zy_guard_ev_already_restricted: already restricted by you, not touched
zy_guard_ev_lifted_in_use: given back: you are using it
zy_guard_ghost_counting: restricted since %1 · %2/day before · after: still counting
zy_guard_ghost_desc: Started in the background %1 or more times over %2 days, never opened, and Android itself marks them idle. Restricting one is the same as choosing "Restricted" in its battery settings: no background work, the app still works when you open it - and opening it gives the background back.
zy_guard_ghost_none: No app qualifies: every app that starts in the background is either opened by you, protected, or still in use according to Android.
zy_guard_ghost_row: %1 background starts in %2 days, never opened
zy_guard_ghost_wait: Suggestions need %1 days of start history; there are %2 so far.
zy_guard_needs_ledger: Needs the process-start ledger: choose Watch or Full above.
zy_guard_nights_note: Process starts of every app, system ones included, between the first and the last screen-off sample of each period of 15 minutes or more.
zy_guard_pending_desc: Dry run: no proposal below has changed AppOps by itself. Confirm only an app whose background work and possible notification delay you accept.
zy_guard_set_off: Restart-loop guard off · every restriction given back
zy_guard_set_wakers: Guard on: restart loops and night wakers
zy_guard_unread: The guard state has not been read yet.
zy_guide_battery_text: Battery guard can restrain proven restart loops after separate observations and your confirmation. Background work and notifications may be delayed; Watch alone does not save power.
zy_guide_minimal_text: Observe only / Watch: diagnostics without frequency requests. Off: no companion work in app processes.
zy_guide_response_text: Launch assist: cold starts only. Response: cold starts + lifecycle hints. Full adds the process journal. These enable requests; they do not guarantee a faster device.
zy_link_apps: Each app: what ASB knows and does (%s)
zy_link_cls_none: no app classed yet - an app needs 3 measured cold starts, or LSPosed modules and one start of a second or more
zy_link_cls_off: off - needs the cold-start lift (Response or Full mode)
zy_link_cmp: Median cold start: apps with LSPosed modules %1 ms (%2 apps), without %3 ms (%4 apps). These are different apps, so the gap is not the cost of the hooks alone.
zy_link_desc: The Zygisk companion hears every app start, LSPosed tells which apps carry hook modules and Android's launch log measures each cold start. From that ASB sorts the apps you open into slow and fast starters: the governor keeps the cold-start lift twice as long for a slow one and ends it at half for a fast one. The background guard never restricts an LSPosed module app.
zy_link_gov_none: not reported by the running governor
zy_link_gov_val: slow starts %1 · fast starts %2 · tap lifts ended early %3
zy_link_lsp_unread: installed; its database could not be read
zy_link_lsp_val: %1 module(s) on · %2 app(s) hooked · framework %3 · System UI %4
zy_link_note: Classes are rebuilt every 30 minutes from the newest data, and an app's class applies from its next cold start. ASB only reads LSPosed and the other Zygisk modules: it never enables, disables or changes them.
zy_link_old_lib: The Zygisk library in use is older than launch classes: they apply once the module's libraries are rebuilt and the phone restarts. Until then every app gets the usual lift.
zy_loading_sub: Loading Zygisk controls and current state. Settings change only after your action.
zy_mode_applied: Mode applied · new app processes pick it up
zy_mode_auto_desc: Cold-start assistance and lifecycle hints for responsiveness, plus the evidence-gated background guard. ART stays separate. This balances mechanisms; it does not promise maximum speed and battery life at once.
zy_mode_battery_desc: Observer and process journal, plus the evidence-gated background guard. Cold-start lifts and lifecycle requests are off. Approved restrictions can delay background work and notifications.
zy_mode_custom_unified: Custom: switches or the guard differ from the preset. ASB will not silently undo your manual choice. Choose a mode above to reapply its complete set.
zy_mode_custom_warning: Manual override active. In particular, cold-start or lifecycle requests added to Battery can increase activity; the interface will not keep calling that set Battery.
zy_mode_note: A change applies to app processes started after it; apps already running keep their state until they restart.
zy_mode_off_desc: Nothing runs in app processes: no connection, no request, no ledger. Zero cost.
zy_mode_performance_desc: Observer, process journal and cold-start assistance. Background guard is off. Existing profile and thermal gates still apply; a faster device is not guaranteed.
zy_mode_safe_note: Safe mode is on: the mode is saved, but nothing runs in app processes until safe mode is cleared below.
zy_mode_speed_desc: Cold-start lift for the app you open, plus a fresh governor reading when an observed app starts or exits. No ledger.
zy_mode_unknown: The current mode could not be read; choosing one writes all four settings.
zy_mode_watch_desc: Process-start ledger and screen-off restart loops for diagnostics. Never touches frequencies; one short companion connection per app process start.
zy_off_desc: ASB will not attach to Zygisk in newly started app processes. Apps that are already running keep their previous state until they are restarted.
zy_off_kept: Your mode, automatic app selection, feature switches, guard and ART settings are preserved. Enabling again restores that setup; it does not silently choose a new preset.
zy_settings_custom: Manual override active; ASB will not silently restore a preset.
zy_status_failed: Could not read the state; the last snapshot is shown
zy_status_failed_empty: Could not read the current Zygisk state. No stale data is shown; reopen the page to try again.
lr_jactive_note: Only ordinary intervals drawing at least 20 FPS. Wake-spanning and near-still intervals are excluded, so a high deadline-miss share on a few waiting frames is not mistaken for scrolling or video stutter.
lr_ltpo_none: No confirmed lower-rate window in this capture
lr_ltpo_none_note: The watcher being enabled does not prove that a compatible video window occurred or that battery was saved. Its decision reason is not exposed by this capture.
lv_drain_on_boot_tip: Battery-level drain with the screen on since this device boot: %s min. Charging and battery-level resets are excluded.
lv_drain_on_boot_wait: needs a battery-level step with the screen on since this device boot
lv_drain_off_night_tip: last proven overnight screen-off stretch: %s; charging and sustained audio excluded
lv_eta_boot_tip: Battery level divided by screen-on drain since this device boot.
lv_drain_on_profile_tip: Latest recorded screen-on drain for this profile: %s min.
lv_drain_off_night_profile_tip: last overnight screen-off stretch recorded while this profile was active: %s
bfx_art_failed: Could not read the list of apps
bfx_art_refused: Android refused every recompile ({fail} of {done} apps), so it was stopped early. Android said: {err}
bfx_art_binder: Android repeatedly rejected both package-scoped compile calls. The run stopped early; unprocessed apps were not counted as compiled, and no all-package fallback or ART/Dalvik cleanup was used. The battery reset is still scheduled. Android said: {err}
bfx_art_scheduled: Immediate recompilation was rejected, so Android’s background optimisation job was started instead. This does not confirm speed-profile compilation; its result will be decided by Android. The battery reset remains scheduled.
bfx_art_partial: Stopped early after repeated Binder refusals: {ok} succeeded, {fail} failed, {left} not attempted. Only package-scoped results are counted; no aggregate success is inferred. The battery reset remains scheduled.
pd_open: Open actual changes for the active profile
kernel_wb_busy: Another wakeup-policy update is finishing; try again
pd_loading: Reading profile intent, live ownership and write readbacks…
pd_error: Could not read current evidence. No setting was changed. Close and try again.
pd_live_title: What is in effect right now
pd_smart_base: Smart inherits these Balanced rails; the live FSM section above shows subsequent dynamic ownership.
pd_intent_note: These are requested rails, not proof of a successful write. Confirm individual outcomes in the readback ledger below.
pd_scope_current: Entries after the latest marker for this profile transaction. Later dynamic adjustments remain visible with their own timestamps.
pd_scope_legacy: No transaction marker from the new version yet. Showing recent legacy rows; apply this profile again for an exact boundary.
pd_no_entries: No ledger entries in this view. Apply the profile again to create a fresh transaction boundary.
pd_evidence_note: Read-only view: no value is changed by opening or refreshing it. “Confirmed” means the recorded readback matched; unsupported or missing evidence is never presented as applied.
pd_smart_note: Adaptive policy: foreground app class and learned app behavior, CPU/GPU load, screen and charging state, battery drain and charging-window budget, network/camera activity, memory pressure, thermal readings and vendor throttling. Night windows and thermal safety vetoes take priority; only validated learned windows are reused, never one fixed limit.
pd_performance_note: Responsiveness first: higher performance headroom, faster ramps and shorter waits for interactive and heavy work.
pd_balanced_note: Everyday middle ground: controlled ramps, bounded background work and moderate CPU/GPU limits.
pd_battery_note: Lower background and idle cost first: conservative ceilings, tighter memory policy and minimal-work I/O preference.
cmp_card_desc: Exact changes made from Infinite Log or added manually share one restoration ledger. Review disabled components, restore them, or add a declared Activity/Service yourself.
cmp_dialog_copy: Restore returns the exact recorded default/enabled state. Entries changed from the Infinite Log report and entries added here share the same list; presence is not proof of battery cost. No automatic component freezing or polling is used.
cmp_empty: No exact Activity/Service changes are saved. Components disabled from Infinite Log appear here as well.
cmp_meta: {n} saved change(s) · Infinite Log and manual entries · one exact restoration ledger
cmp_add_note: Enter a declared full package/Class. Android must prove its declaration and original state; disable still requires a second tap and read-back. This does not freeze the app or create a Worker/Service alias.
cmp_add_invalid: Enter a valid full package/Class and choose Activity or Service
cmp_not_declared: The exact declared component or its original state could not be proven; nothing was changed
dsp_eq_desc: Three independent parametric bands for Speaker, Wired and Bluetooth. Frequency, Q and gain are stored separately. Zero gain disables a band.
dsp_eq_output_desc: Selects which independently stored EQ you are editing.
dsp_eq_gain_desc: Range −12…+12 dB. Zero bypasses this band.
kernel_wb_dialog_hint_raw: Raw event/activation counters can keep increasing while a rule works: they describe source attempts, not successful wakeups. Only the active kernel rule and its blocked counter prove blocking. A screen-off rule is inactive while the screen is on. These are not energy measurements.
kernel_wb_source_metrics_raw: Raw kernel counters: +{events} events · +{active} activations · +{time} active
kernel_wb_rule_active_blocked: Rule active now · blocked by this rule: {n}
kernel_wb_rule_active_stats_unknown: Rule active now · per-rule blocked counter not exposed
kernel_wb_rule_waiting_screen_off: Saved for screen-off only · inactive while the screen is on or its state is unknown
kernel_wb_rule_readback_missing: Saved, but absent from the current kernel readback
lr_activity_head: Activity context in high-drain screen-on phases (8%/h or more, at least 5 min):
lr_activity_note: Components were observed at the start/end of the phase. This correlation does not prove that an activity caused the drain; freezing it can break the app. No activity is named when Android did not expose one.
lv_drain_on_avg_tip: Average screen-on drain of this profile: %s min measured.
lv_drain_note_src: Screen on: the active profile’s drain in this boot (since boot, or since the profile was selected) once it covers at least as much screen-on time as its latest session, otherwise the latest complete session (two battery-level steps, or 30 min with one), otherwise the profile average; the heading names which one. Charging time is left out. The table below holds each profile’s average, so the active profile’s row can differ from the figure above. Right now is only the latest continuous stretch. Screen off prefers the latest confirmed night. All figures come from the battery level, not from the current sensor.
lv_drain_on_switch_tip: Battery-level drain with the screen on since this profile was selected in this boot: %s min. Charging and battery-level resets are excluded.
